extra.message: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in ops dock spool endpoint — Arbitrary file write to any location on the filesystem, leading to code execution or system compromise [verified: The 'packet_ref' query parameter is concatenated with incoming_dir via Path '/' operator at line 26 and the raw request body is written to that path with no sanitization, allowing path traversal outside the intended directory.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in ops Jinja2 endpoint — Remote code execution, reading server-side secrets and environment variables [verified: The 'fragment' query parameter is string-concatenated into a Jinja2 Template('Result: ' + fragment) at line 97 and rendered with no escaping or sandbox; attacker-supplied Jinja2 expressions execute with full Python access.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in ops dock shelf endpoint — Arbitrary file write to any location on the filesystem, leading to code execution or system compromise [verified: The 'name' query parameter is concatenated with BASE_EXPORT_DIR via Path '/' operator at line 103 and the raw request body is written to that path with no path sanitization, enabling arbitrary file writes via traversal sequences.]

OS Command Injection in ops shell probe endpoint — Remote code execution on the server with the application's privileges [verified: The 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into 'ping -c 1 ' + host and passed to os.system() at line 111 with zero sanitization; the _wrk_gate dependency provides authentication but no input validation, leaving command injection fully exploitable by anyone who passes the gate.]

No rate limiting on authentication endpoints — brute-force possible — Credential brute-forcing — attacker can make unlimited login attempts to guess passwords or enumerate valid accounts without being blocked. [verified: Same finding as idx 2: no rate-limiting exists on any auth endpoint (login, register, password-reset-request), permitting unlimited brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint — Brute-force password guessing against user accounts, leading to account takeover [verified: No rate limiting middleware or guard exists anywhere in the codebase (confirmed by exhaustive search); the /api/auth/login endpoint accepts email+password with no brute-force protection, enabling unlimited credential guessing.]

Mass assignment in ticket update — staff can reassign ticket team ownership — Cross-team data leakage — staff can move tickets to other teams, potentially exposing sensitive ticket data to unauthorized teams after the reassignment. [verified: TicketUpdate schema includes team_id/assigned_agent_id/queue_id; update_ticket checks ensure_ticket_work before the setattr loop (line 374), so a staff user whose team matches the ticket's current team can set team_id to any value, moving the ticket to an unauthorized team and exposing sensitive data to that team's members.]

Unvalidated file upload — trusts client content-type without content inspection — Malicious file hosting — attacker can upload malware, phishing pages, or executable content that gets served with attacker-controlled MIME type. [verified: Same finding as idx 3: upload_attachment trusts client content_type and preserves original extension with no server-side content inspection, allowlist, or size cap; downloadable with attacker-chosen MIME type.]

Unrestricted File Upload — trusts client content-type and preserves extension — Upload of executable or malicious files with spoofed content-types; potential stored XSS via HTML files served with the attacker-supplied MIME type. [verified: File upload at line 443 trusts client-supplied content_type verbatim and uses the original filename extension (line 431) with no magic-byte inspection, allowlist, or size limit; download_attachment at line 455 serves with attacker-controlled media_type, enabling stored-XSS via HTML files or malware hosting.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — transmitted over unencrypted HTTP — Session hijacking — an active network attacker on the same network can intercept session cookies and impersonate users. [verified: Same underlying issue as idx 0 — create_session() at security.py:29-30 hardcodes secure=False with no compensating HTTPS enforcement, allowing network attackers to sniff session cookies and hijack accounts.]

CORS Misconfiguration — Reflected Origin with Credentials — Cross-origin requests with credentials from any attacker-controlled origin, enabling session theft [verified: The endpoint echoes the request's Origin header as Access-Control-Allow-Origin at line 87 with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true at line 88, allowing any attacker-controlled origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and steal session cookies.]

NoSQL Injection via raw MongoDB query — Arbitrary MongoDB document access, potential code execution via $where operator [verified: The JSON body is passed directly as a MongoDB query via payload.get('filter', payload) to find_one() at line 138 with no operator whitelisting or sanitization, enabling arbitrary NoSQL operators including $where.]

User enumeration via registration endpoint — reveals existing accounts — Account enumeration — attacker can compile a list of valid user emails for targeted password spraying or phishing attacks. [verified: Same finding as idx 1: registration returns distinct 409/201 responses for existing vs new emails with no timing normalization or rate-limiting, enabling reliable user enumeration.]

CSV formula injection in report export with user-controlled ticket subjects — Code execution in spreadsheet applications — when an admin opens the exported CSV, malicious formulas can execute commands or exfiltrate data from the admin's machine. [verified: Same finding as idx 0: ticket subjects and escalation reasons reach csv.DictWriter.writerows() unsanitized at the export_report endpoint; no formula-injection-character filtering anywhere in the chain.]

Open Redirect in ops after lane endpoint — Phishing and credential theft by redirecting users to attacker-controlled domains [verified: The 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(lane) at line 44 with no URL validation or whitelist check, allowing redirection to arbitrary attacker-controlled domains.]

Sensitive Data Exposure — Authorization Bearer Token Logged in Plaintext — Exposure of valid session tokens or API keys to log consumers, enabling account takeover [verified: The Authorization header value is logged in plaintext via logger.warning at line 56, writing bearer tokens (session tokens or API keys) to application logs accessible to operators with log access.]

Denial of Service via Unbounded JSON Array Generation — Server memory exhaustion and denial of service for all users [verified: The 'count' query parameter is passed directly to range(count) at line 69 with no upper bound, allowing an attacker who passes the gate to exhaust server memory by requesting arbitrarily large arrays.]

Information Disclosure — Environment Variables and Internal Paths Exposed — Exposure of internal configuration and directory structure, aiding reconnaissance and targeted attacks [verified: The endpoint at line 131 returns os.environ.get('APP_ENV') and str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in its JSON response, disclosing internal environment configuration and directory paths.]

Hardcoded default database credentials and session secret — Full compromise — attacker can connect to the database directly or forge session tokens to impersonate any user if the defaults are not overridden in production. [verified: The database_url default ('supportdesk:supportdesk@localhost:5433') IS hardcoded and used by create_engine if SUPPORT_DESK_DATABASE_URL is unset, though it targets localhost and is overridable via documented env var; the session_secret default is dead code — never imported or used by any module (sessions use secrets.token_urlsafe random tokens, not signed JWTs), so session forgery via this value i]

Overly permissive CORS regex with credentials — any localhost port allowed — Cross-origin data theft — a malicious page on any localhost port can make authenticated API requests, exfiltrating user data and performing actions as the victim. [verified: CORS regex r'http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1):\d+' with allow_credentials=True permits any localhost-port origin to make credentialed requests; samesite=lax treats all localhost ports as same-site so cookies are sent — but exploitation requires a malicious page already served from a localhost port, implying local code execution or a compromised local service.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Password Reset Endpoint — Abuse of password-reset token generation, potential resource exhaustion and user harassment [verified: No rate limiting exists on /api/auth/password-reset/request, but the endpoint always returns a uniform response (no user enumeration) and generates only mock tokens with no actual email delivery — the only real impact is database resource exhaustion.]

Missing Authentication on Sensitive Ops Endpoint (fold-060) — Unauthenticated access to sensitive business intelligence and ticket metadata [verified: This is the only ops endpoint lacking the gate_ref=Depends(_wrk_gate) dependency at line 38, making it publicly accessible without authentication; the returned data is hardcoded mock values rather than real sensitive data, so impact is limited.]

Information Disclosure via Verbose Error Response — Exposure of internal filesystem paths and application internals, facilitating further attacks [verified: A deliberately raised RuntimeError including the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR path is returned in the JSON response body at line 77, exposing internal filesystem structure to callers.]
